reason: The text describes external adversaries (Sanballat, Tobiah, and enemies) mocking and threatening the Jewish builders. The Jewish people themselves express exhaustion about the work ('the strength of the laborers is failing'), and they report threats from enemies. However, the Hebrew leaders (represented by Nehemiah) respond with encouragement, organizational action, and defensive measures to support the people. The leaders organize half the people to work while the other half stands guard with weapons, and Nehemiah exhorts the people not to be afraid. There is no instance of the Hebrew leaders complaining about the people—rather, the leadership narrative shows support and strategic organization in response to the people's difficulties and external threats.
